summary: Modern databases and data platforms increasingly embed AI/ML directly into their engines, offering in-database model training, LLM access, and vector similarity search so data never leaves the governed platform. Native vector search is now a key differentiator—some platforms (Databricks, MongoDB Atlas, BigQuery) offer it built-in, while others rely on extensions like pgvector. Snowflake's recent launch of Snowflake Postgres with Cortex AI reflects a broader convergence of operational databases, analytics, and generative AI on unified, secure platforms.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Snowflake Cortex AI (LLM functions, Cortex Search, Cortex Analyst, embeddings)
databases.description: Cortex AI provides serverless access to hosted LLMs and embedding models through SQL/Python functions (COMPLETE, SUMMARIZE, TRANSLATE, SENTIMENT, EXTRACT_ANSWER), plus Cortex Search for RAG and Cortex Analyst for natural-language querying. With Snowflake Postgres, these capabilities now extend to Postgres-based operational applications without managing AI infrastructure.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native built-in vector search via the VECTOR data type and vector similarity functions (VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY, etc.) plus the managed Cortex Search service; no third-party extension required.
databases.llm_integration: Native, first-party LLM access to models from Anthropic (Claude), Meta (Llama), Mistral, OpenAI, and Snowflake Arctic via Cortex functions; no external API keys needed.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based pricing measured in Snowflake credits; Cortex LLM functions billed per token/credit based on model size, separate from standard warehouse compute.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML with Vertex AI and Gemini integration
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets users create and run ML models (regression, classification, clustering, time series, boosted trees) using standard SQL. It integrates with Vertex AI to call remote generative models (Gemini) and embedding models directly from SQL via ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native built-in vector search via the VECTOR_SEARCH function and CREATE VECTOR INDEX; supports IVF/TreeAH indexes natively within BigQuery.
databases.llm_integration: Native integration with Vertex AI foundation models (Gemini, text-embedding models) accessible through SQL functions on remote model endpoints.
databases.pricing_notes: On-demand pricing per bytes processed or capacity-based (slots) for queries; generative/embedding calls incur additional Vertex AI model usage charges.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.ai_feature: pgvector extension for vectors and pgai for in-database LLM/embedding workflows
databases.description: Open-source PostgreSQL gains AI capabilities through extensions: pgvector adds vector storage and similarity search, while pgai (from Timescale) enables calling LLM and embedding APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, etc.) directly from SQL and automating embedding pipelines with pgvectorscale for performance.
databases.vector_search_notes: Vector search is available but NOT part of core PostgreSQL—it requires the pgvector extension (with optional pgvectorscale). Because core PostgreSQL has no built-in vector type, this is extension-based, though pgvector is first-class open-source and nearly ubiquitous in managed Postgres offerings.
databases.llm_integration: No native LLM access in core Postgres; the pgai extension enables calling external LLM/embedding providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, Ollama) from SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: pgvector and pgai are free open-source extensions; cost depends on the hosting environment (self-managed or managed Postgres service) plus any external LLM API usage fees.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.ai_feature: Aurora Machine Learning (integration with Amazon SageMaker, Bedrock, and Comprehend)
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you add ML-based predictions to applications using SQL by calling out to Amazon SageMaker endpoints, Amazon Bedrock (generative models/embeddings), and Amazon Comprehend for sentiment analysis—without building custom integrations or moving data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Aurora PostgreSQL does not have native vector search in its core engine; vector similarity requires the pgvector extension installed on Aurora PostgreSQL. Since it depends on a third-party/open-source extension rather than a built-in capability, this is marked false.
databases.llm_integration: Native SQL-level integration with Amazon Bedrock foundation models and SageMaker-hosted models, allowing LLM and embedding generation from within Aurora.
databases.pricing_notes: Standard Aurora instance/storage/I-O pricing; ML inference incurs separate charges for the invoked SageMaker, Bedrock, or Comprehend services.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.ai_feature: Redshift ML (in-warehouse model training and inference via SQL + SageMaker/Bedrock)
databases.description: Redshift ML enables analysts to create, train, and deploy ML models using familiar SQL CREATE MODEL statements, leveraging Amazon SageMaker Autopilot under the hood. It also supports bringing custom SageMaker models and invoking Bedrock LLMs for generative tasks from SQL.
databases.vector_search_notes: Redshift does not offer a native, first-class vector index/search engine comparable to dedicated vector databases; it has limited support for similarity computations but no built-in managed vector search, so this is marked false.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock and SageMaker for generative and predictive inference invoked directly from SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: Charged via Redshift compute (RPU/node) pricing; model training via SageMaker Autopilot and LLM inference via Bedrock are billed separately on their respective services.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI (model training, serving, agents) and Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Databricks Mosaic AI provides end-to-end GenAI tooling—foundation model APIs, fine-tuning, model serving, agent frameworks, and governance via Unity Catalog. Databricks Vector Search delivers a fully managed vector database integrated with the Lakehouse for RAG applications.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native built-in managed Vector Search service that automatically syncs with Delta tables and provides serverless vector indexes; no external extension required.
databases.llm_integration: Native access to foundation models through Mosaic AI Model Serving and Foundation Model APIs (including Llama, DBRX, and external providers), plus fine-tuning and agent orchestration.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based using Databricks Units (DBUs); Vector Search and Model Serving are billed as separate serverless compute line items based on usage.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search and Atlas AI integrations
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search enables semantic/similarity search over embeddings stored alongside operational documents, powering RAG and AI applications directly within the database. It integrates with popular AI frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex) and embedding providers.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native built-in vector search implemented as a managed index type ($vectorSearch aggregation stage) within Atlas; no third-party extension needed, with HNSW indexing supported natively.
databases.llm_integration: No hosted first-party LLM; integrates with external embedding and LLM providers (OpenAI, Cohere, Hugging Face, AWS Bedrock, Google) and AI frameworks for building RAG pipelines.
databases.pricing_notes: Included within Atlas cluster pricing; vector search runs on dedicated Search Nodes or shared cluster resources, billed as part of Atlas tiered/consumption compute and storage.
